event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: The filing demonstrates that COVID-19 continues to be a meaningful—but now moderating—risk driver for WST. Four years after the official declaration of the pandemic, the company is still recording tangible financial consequences: a US$320 million drop in proprietary product sales and a US$21 million reduction in COVID-19 supply-agreement fees. These are realized, quantified impacts, not merely hypothetical exposures, confirming that the pandemic has materially compressed revenue and margins. At the same time, the risk narrative has shifted from acute crisis management to a more blended outlook that combines lingering demand erosion with generic forward-looking cautions about future “pandemic” disruptions to manufacturing and supply chains. Because the event is now just beyond the three-year “recent” window, the Time Decay Principle tempers severity: evidence is scored in the moderate range (4-6) rather than the extreme range (7-10). Overall, the disclosures reflect both historical financial damage and an ongoing, though less pronounced, operational vulnerability tied to future global health crises.

evidence_list.snippet: The functioning of our manufacturing and distribution assets and systems could be disrupted for reasons either within or beyond our control, including, without limitation: extreme weather, water scarcity and other longer-term climatic changes; natural or man-made disasters; pandemic; war; accidental damage; disruption to the supply of material or services; product quality and safety issues; systems failure; workforce actions; or environmental matters.

components.reason: Explicitly lists ‘pandemic’ as a potential disruption factor.
Links pandemic to disruption of manufacturing and distribution—core operations.
Presented as part of a broad catch-all list, reducing specificity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic but clear acknowledgement that a pandemic could disrupt critical operations; moderately severe given lack of specificity and four-year time decay.

evidence_list.snippet: Excluding foreign currency translation effects and the impact related to the disposal of one of our plants of $11.5 million, net sales decreased by $20.1 million, or 0.8%, primarily due to a decline in COVID-related sales of approximately $320 million, offset by growth in our high-value components, primarily Westar ® , Daikyo ® and Envision ® , as well as growth in high-value devices, such as self-injection systems and administration systems, and sales price increases.

components.reason: Direct causal link between COVID and sales decline (‘primarily due to a decline in COVID-related sales’).
Quantifies a large, material impact (≈US$320 million).
Reflects realized, historical impact rather than hypothetical.
Mentions offsetting growth in other areas, partially mitigating effect.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Substantial, quantified revenue hit directly tied to COVID; time decay limits score to upper-moderate range.

evidence_list.snippet: The decrease is driven by a decline in higher margin COVID-related sales, a decrease of approximately $21 million, net, in fees received from COVID-19 supply agreements, and inflationary pressures, primarily within compensation costs.

components.reason: Directly attributes profit decline to reduced COVID-related sales and fees.
Provides specific dollar figure (US$21 million) for the COVID fee reduction.
Highlights impact on higher-margin items, signalling profitability sensitivity.
Blends COVID effect with other factors (inflation), diluting exclusivity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows meaningful, quantified profitability impact linked to COVID, but coexistence with inflationary factors moderates severity.
